questions.q: For the given molecule x, the preferred site for the attack of the electrophile is:
questions.explain: The molecule has two rings, so first decide which one is more reactive. The ring on N gets electrons from the N lone pair by +M, so it is activated and directs ortho/para. That lone pair is also shared with the C=O, so this is weaker than in aniline, but it still wins. The ring on the C=O side is deactivated by the C=O group (-M). So the attack is on the N-ring. Between ortho (s) and para (u), para is less crowded, so the answer is predominantly at u.

questions.q: Method used for separation of the mixture of products B and C obtained in the following reaction is:
questions.explain: Br is an ortho/para director, so nitrating bromobenzene gives o-bromonitrobenzene and p-bromonitrobenzene. These two isomers have different boiling points, so fractional distillation can separate them. Steam distillation only works when one isomer is steam-volatile through intramolecular H-bonding (like o-nitrophenol), which is not the case here. Simple distillation is too crude for close-boiling isomers, and sublimation does not fit.

questions.q: Consider the compounds a, b and c. Arrange these compounds in the increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture.
questions.explain: Nitration is faster when the ring has more electron density. OCH3 (c) donates strongly by +M, so it is the fastest. Cl (a) pulls by -I more than it donates by +M, so it is a little deactivated. NO2 (b) pulls by both -M and -I, so it is strongly deactivated and the slowest. So b < a < c.

questions.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with CH3COCl/AlCl3 will give m-nitroacetophenone. Statement II: -NO2 group is a m-directing, and deactivating group. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explain: Check each statement by itself. NO2 is strongly electron withdrawing, so the ring is too electron poor for Friedel-Crafts acylation. Statement I is therefore incorrect. NO2 pulls electrons by -M and -I, and the pull is strongest at ortho and para. That leaves meta as the least deactivated position, so NO2 is a deactivating, meta-directing group. Statement II is correct.
